speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: To enhance career opportunities for our local workforce, we have acted on four fronts: first, transforming our economy to be more innovative, productive and manpower-lean so that we can remain competitive and create enough good jobs for our people; second, strengthening lifelong learning through the SkillsFuture movement so as to enhance the employability of our local workforce throughout their working life; third, helping more local professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) under the Adapt and Grow (A&G) initiative to adapt better to the rapid pace of technological change so that they can grow in their current careers or switch to new careers; and last but not least, raising the qualifying criteria of Employment Pass and strengthening the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) so as to improve the complementarity of local and foreign PMETs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Our economy has become more manpower-lean and our workforce more productive.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: What is even more encouraging is that productivity growth has also improved to 1% last year, after remaining flat since 2012.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: With even higher productivity growth this year than last year, we are making steady progress towards our medium-term growth strategy of 1% growth in manpower and 2% growth in productivity for a 3% growth in gross domestic product (GDP) per annum.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: From this diagram (Annex A), Members can see that we are making a transition from a "4+0=4" situation, which means 4% manpower growth and 0% increase in productivity, towards the growth strategy of "1+2=3".

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Over the last few years, we have been making steady progress towards that outcome.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The PMET share of the resident workforce has also improved in the last three years from 53.5% in 2014 to 56.1% in 2017.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, 56% of the resident workforce today is doing PMET jobs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The rate of increase is at a faster rate than the previous three years.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: What is also worth noting is the share of nett PMET employment growth that went to our local PMETs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This faster rate of increase in our medium wage is a reflection of improvement in the quality of jobs for our resident workforce.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Moving forward, there is still much to do to create more and better job opportunities for our local workforce.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Unemployment and long-term unemployment rates have risen, though marginally, in past two years.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We need to, first, bring total employment growth up to about 25,000 to 40,000 a year to keep unemployment down; second, improve the quality of jobs to minimise under-employment; and third, minimise job-skills mismatches so as to prevent unemployment from becoming structural and sticky.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Our economic agencies and tripartite partners will continue to transform industries, from manufacturing to services and construction.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, Singaporeans can look forward to good jobs that harness technology in artificial intelligence in infocomm and media, data analytics in electronics manufacturing, financial technology (FinTech) in finance and banking, and prefabrication technology in construction.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: More industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) will be launched progressively in the coming months.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Together, we aim to achieve and sustain nett employment growth of about 25,000 to 40,000 a year.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is lower than the high job growth of 120,000 a year three to five years ago which was not sustainable, but is higher than the low job growth of less than 10,000 last year.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: More importantly, through these ITMs, we aim to improve the quality of jobs pervasively across all sectors, in other words, to make every job a better job.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We will also continue to strengthen the SkillsFuture movement to equip our people with the skills needed for the future economy, in other words, to make every worker a better worker.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For instance, the Ministry of Education (MOE) recently announced the SkillsFuture Series to provide working adults with industry-relevant skills in eight priority and emerging skills areas that draw reference from the ITMs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM), together with our tripartite partners, will press on with our A&G efforts to support more local PMETs of all ages from all industries to grow in their current careers or pursue new career opportunities in new and key growth sectors.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We will also help speed up the transfer of advanced and emerging expertise from outside of Singapore to our local workforce through the newly launched Capability Transfer Programme.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Beyond these efforts of the Government and the tripartite partners, our local PMETs must be prepared to adapt and grow to stay relevant and seize new opportunities.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Likewise, employers must also do their part to be inclusive and adopt fair and progressive hiring practices.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In this regard, I am encouraged that more local PMETs and more employers are making good use of A&G programmes.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In the first half of this year, about 1,500 local PMETs have undergone skills conversion through Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs).

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is more than double that in the same period last year.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Likewise, in the first six months of this year, nearly 1,500 employers participated in A&G programmes, such as the PCPs and P-MAX.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is almost the total number for the whole of last year.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, they found jobs after being unemployed for longer than six months.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This inclusive profile of job placement is, indeed, encouraging.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We will keep doing more, doing better for local PMETs and our local workforce.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I am sure the Minister would agree with me that one of the most urgent priorities is to help displaced mid-career persons.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Many of them still have mortgages to pay, children still going to school and they have 20 to 25 years more of productive working life.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The Minister did share some encouraging updates in terms of numbers.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: On the ground, the sense is that there are still a lot of challenges and hardship faced by many of these families.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Please give us some sense of what that 1,500 successful cases represent, what is this as a percentage of the total population that the Ministry is still helping?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is the reason why under our A&G initiative, we pay particular attention to the PMETs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Among the PMETs affected, those who are more than 40 years old, or the mid-career mature PMETs, our concern is that they may need more support to remain employable.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is the reason why we have been enhancing our support for the mature PMETs in our A&G programmes.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I want to point out that the number of PMETs that we have helped is more than the 1,500 that went through the PCP.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As I had mentioned earlier, in the first eight months of this year, we have helped 16,000 local jobseekers to secure jobs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, if we take 58% of 16,000, we will come to almost 10,000 local PMETs who managed to secure jobs with the help provided for under the A&G programmes.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Of the 10,000 who successfully found jobs, not every one of them needed to go through professional conversion.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: There is a split between missed-match and mismatch.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Missed-match means they are job ready except that they need some help to secure jobs through our job-matching services.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Only for those who face difficulty in the mismatch of skill, wage expectation and so on, we would help them with the Career Support Programme (CSP) and PCP.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I would say that by looking ahead into the future, we expect the proportion of PMETs who have to overcome mismatch is going to continue to grow.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: That is the reason why we continue to expand PCP to more and more sectors.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I expect the number of PMETs participating in PCP to continue to grow.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: These sectors are finance and banking, infocomm and media, healthcare, wholesale trade and professional services.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: These five sectors combined together will account for 60% of the PMET job creation in the medium term.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: MOM is, therefore, working closely with the respective economic agencies and Ministries to see how we can step up our efforts to help: firstly, more of the PMETs in these five sectors to remain employable within their companies, what we call in-company PCP, so that even though their jobs are at risk today, we can help them to update their skills and remain employable within the same company; secondly, for those who for whatever reasons are being affected by company redundancy, to help them to remain in the same industry, and so there is an intra-sector PCP; and thirdly, to help those who are affected by redundancy elsewhere to convert and come into these growing sectors through inter-sector PCP.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In the coming months, Members can expect to see many more initiatives being launched.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I just have a question to ask or one suggestion to make.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Yes, the ITMs have raised quite a few growth sectors, in particular, the five mentioned, but I also notice that for many of these growth sectors, most of these jobs require skills that are pretty specialised and so there are quite a bit of "barriers to entry".

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Yes, initial efforts have been promising, but I hope the Ministry, together with our tripartite partners, can do even more, in particular, to plug this gap, and make it more pervasive.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Also, for the employers, some mindsets have to change.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: They will not be able to get "plug-and-play" people, but they can be more open to hiring so that, as what the Minister shared earlier, we can not only make every job a better job and every worker a better worker, but also every employer a better employer.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In the future, under the ITM, we can expect to see more and more sectors requiring advanced and specialised skills.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: And yet, at the same time, we also need to inculcate in our PMETs the ability to adapt.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, they have to re-specialise within their job sectors and their career and, at the same time, they must be prepared to keep re-specialising repeatedly.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I also fully agree that tripartite partnership is very important in changing the mindset of the employer, changing the mindset of the worker.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: At the end of the day, we can only truly succeed if we are able to get every employer to come on board to make every job a better job, and if we are able to get every worker to come on board to adapt and grow so that we can make every worker a better worker.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: And hopefully, through our tripartite partners, we can match every better job to every better worker, and every better worker to every job, so that we do not have a problem with unemployment, under-employment and structural unemployment.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: With regard to the Government's four-prong strategy to improve career opportunities for PMETs, can I ask the Minister what have been the main challenges and limitations for the Government in pursuing new initiatives to improve career opportunities for PMETs, and what have been the downsides of the Ministry's efforts?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: What does it intend to do to urge individuals to take the Ministry's plans a bit more seriously?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The pace of the restructuring, obviously, is not even across all sectors, across all companies.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But what has happened in the last few years, as I had mentioned earlier, is that through this four-prong approach, our economy has become more manpower-lean.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As a result, more and more companies have come to the realisation that counting on manpower-driven growth, as it was the past, is no longer relevant in future.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, we are seeing more companies now preparing to transform instead of coming to MOM to ask us to relax on the foreign worker policy.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In fact, more and more of them are now coming forward to ask us what we can do to help them to become manpower-lean.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: One example is the Lean Enterprise Development (LED) scheme launched last year.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The purpose of the LED scheme is to encourage more and more small and medium enterprises (SMEs), in particular, to become more manpower-lean and to become more resource-lean, rather than to keep asking for more foreign workers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, we are seeing a very healthy increase.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This coming Friday, we are holding our second annual symposium on the LED scheme where the tripartite partners will be coming together to take stock of what we have achieved together in the last two years, and how we can do even more moving forward.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, up to now, we help mainly company by company, enterprise by enterprise.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We are now looking at how we can get groups of companies to come together, so that instead of just working on the development of Lean Enterprise, we can work together towards the development of Lean Industry.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, we learn together, adapt together and grow together.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Retrenchment has gone up in the last two years.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: What the tripartite partners – the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC), MOM, together with the Singapore National Employers Federation (SNEF) – did was we formed a retrenchment response task force.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: What this task force does is, firstly, we monitor whether the retrenchment was done in a responsible manner.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The support that we have provided is not just to SPH.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We have extended the same level of support to all the workers affected by retrenchments since last year.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: In terms of the 10,000 PMETs who were successfully helped, again, I just want to have a sense of the dimension of the problem on the ground.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: What was the proportion helped, compared to the overall base?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: How many more do we need to help?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: How many out there do we need to find good careers for?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Of this 2.2 million, on the average, every year, about 180,000 to 200,000 would leave our resident workforce.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: It could be for retirement, further studies or to take a break from their job and career and so on.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: At the same time, about the same number, 180,000 to 200,000 would re-enter the workforce.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, people who go for further studies come back to work; people who took a break and come back to work.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, every year, if you look at the turnover of our resident workforce, it is about 180,000 to 200,000.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Of the 180,000 to 200,000 who come back to the workforce, not all of them would need help from Workforce Singapore (WSG) or the Employment and Employability Institute (e2i).

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In fact, the vast majority are able to find employment on their own.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, for every three local PMETs who need job placement assistance from WSG or e2i, we are able to successfully secure jobs for two out of three.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For the other one-third, even though we are not able to succeed in getting job placements for them, it does not mean that all of them would remain unemployed.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Some of them will go on on their own to find their own jobs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I hope this will give the Member the big picture.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Minister help by sharing the statistics on the success rate by ethnicities of PMETs, especially for the Malay community?
